title: New Reformed divisions: Tilenus's decreeing and executing grace
source_text: XXV. Sed praeter solennes illas gratiae divisiones usitatas in Schola Rom. multae sunt a Doctoribus Reformatis excogitatae. Sic Tilenus Dei gratiam distinguit in decernentem atque exequentem. Illa, inquit, denotat aeternum Dei propositum de nobis eligendis ante jacta mundi fundamenta: Ista complectitur totam admirandi hujus mysterii oeconomiam, secundum temporum ac graduum varietatem. De divinae voluntatis nominibus disp. 1. th. 24.
pass_a_gloss: XXV. But besides those solemn divisions of grace usual in the Rom. School many have been devised by the Reformed Doctors. Thus Tilenus distinguishes the grace of God into decreeing and executing. The former, he says, denotes the eternal purpose of God concerning electing us before the foundations of the world were laid: The latter embraces the whole economy of this admirable mystery, according to the variety of times and degrees. On the names of the divine will disp. 1. th. 24.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXV. Besides the standard divisions of grace used in the Roman school, the Reformed doctors have devised many of their own. Tilenus, for example, distinguishes God's grace into decreeing and executing grace.

The first, he says, means God's eternal purpose to choose us before the foundations of the world were laid. The second covers the whole working out of this wonderful mystery through its various times and stages (On the names of the divine will, disputation 1, thesis 24).
